Introduction

Learn how one country can have a capital city, old places, sea cities, islands, food, writing, and daily life.

What picture comes to your mind when you hear this country name?

Do you know Seoul, Korean food, Korean music, or Korean TV stories?

Can one small country have many different local places?

Practice

Why is this country more than one famous picture?

Because it has cities, old places, islands, food, writing, and daily life.

What famous picture do you know?

What is a peninsula?

A peninsula is land with water on three sides.

Which place sounds more interesting to you: a capital city, a sea city, an island, or mountains?

What can you see in Seoul?

You can see modern city life and old history together.

Do you like cities with old places and new places?

Why is the country not only Seoul?

Busan, Jeju, Gyeongju, and other places have different local stories.

Which place can you remember, and why?

What is Hangeul?

Hangeul is the Korean writing system.

What writing, food, or public place helps explain your country?

What is one better question than "What is it famous for?

One better question is "What is local here?

Explain the country without using only music or TV stories.

Summary

South Korea is a small country with many local worlds.

Seoul shows old and new city life.

Busan shows a sea city and port.

Jeju shows island nature.

Gyeongju shows old history.

Hangeul shows writing and daily culture.

Food, markets, rivers, and public places show everyday life.

The main idea is simple: do not stop at the famous picture.

Ask what is local.

See the map, the city, the island, the food, the writing, and the speed of daily life.

Then the country becomes clearer in English.
